title: Pentagon Ousts Top Military Strategist as Trump Considers Escalating Iran Strikes
snippet: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has fired Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, the Pentagon's chief planner, as President Trump weighs new military action against Iran.
content:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has ousted Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, the Pentagon's top military strategist, as President Donald Trump considers launching new military strikes against Iran. Sylvia's sudden departure marks the latest high-profile shakeup in a continuing overhaul of senior defense leadership.

Sylvia served as head of strategy, plans, and policy on the Joint Chiefs of Staff—a crucial role known in military circles as the 'J5'—where he was tasked with developing and coordinating global military strategy for both the chairman of the Joint Chiefs and the White House. He is the second general removed from the position under Hegseth's leadership, following the forced retirement of Lt. Gen. Joseph McGee last fall. A defense official, speaking on condition of anonymity, confirmed the firing but noted that no rationale was given and no replacement has been named.

Strategic Turmoil Amid Growing Regional Conflict

The firing comes at a delicate time for U.S. national security. President Trump has repeatedly signaled a desire to expand military operations against Iran following next week's midterm elections, promising to 'finish the job' in an eight-month-long regional conflict. U.S. diplomats have advised several Middle Eastern allies to prepare for prospective strikes as well as potential retaliation from Tehran. In preparation, the U.S. is deploying a third aircraft carrier and thousands of extra troops to the region.

Part of a Broader Senior Leadership Reduction

Sylvia is the latest of nearly two dozen general officers, admirals, and top military secretaries to be removed or forced out during Hegseth's tenure. Hegseth has defended the sweeping changes as part of a directive to slash the total number of general and flag officers by 20 percent, calling the move a long-overdue drive for accountability.

However, the rapid departures have drawn sharp backlash from Capitol Hill. Critics, including Sen. Mark Kelly (D-Ariz.), a former Navy combat pilot, have characterized the moves as a political purge that risks draining the armed forces of vital institutional expertise and strategic leadership for years to come.
